title: Reorganize into multiple teams
summary: Configure Linear/Jira with multiple teams, cross-team dependencies, roadmap views, and sprint cadences.

parts.title: Create teams for each department
parts.guidance: Map the agreed departments and membership roster onto the tracker, identifying teams that will be retained, renamed, split, or retired. Preserve the ownership of active projects and decide where ongoing work moves before changing the structure. Create the new teams and access groups, then move work using that mapping. Give team leads a view of their resulting backlog and call out tasks that lost an owner or became inaccessible.

parts.title: Configure workflow states per team
parts.guidance: Map each department's intake, execution, review, and completion stages. Keep common meanings where cross-team reporting depends on them, and allow different states where the work genuinely differs. Build an old-to-new status mapping for active issues before changing workflows. Walk current tasks through the new states with their team leads, resolve ambiguous transitions, and then move the existing queue so work retains an understandable status.

parts.title: Create cross-team projects
parts.guidance: Identify outcomes that require several departments and name one accountable project owner for each. Agree the contributing teams, deliverables, dependencies, and handoff points. Link the contributing teams' existing tasks into the shared project. Give participating leads a view that shows their responsibilities and the next cross-team dependency, and resolve any deliverable that appears to have two owners or none.

parts.title: Set up sprint cycles
parts.guidance: Choose a planning cadence that fits each team's workload and release needs. Agree how it handles unplanned work, dependencies, and tasks left unfinished at the end of a cycle. Configure the supported cycle settings and put the next set of work into them. Check capacity and dates with the team lead, then document how unfinished work moves into the next cycle and affects its plan.

parts.title: Create Slack channel integrations
parts.guidance: For teams using Slack, choose which tracker events warrant a channel message and where those messages belong. Check channel membership against the linked issues' visibility and review the integration's permissions with the administrators before connecting it. Trigger a representative event and inspect the message, link access, and duplicates. Adjust noisy rules before expanding the integration, and tell the channel owner how to change or disable notifications.

parts.title: Document process in Notion
parts.guidance: Document the new operating model in the team's wiki, using Notion if selected. Explain team ownership, intake routes, workflow meanings, planning cadence, and cross-team handoffs, linking the tracker views people should use. Include a concrete example of a request that crosses departments and show who owns each handoff. Ask the involved leads to resolve gaps, then share the guide and identify who updates it as the organization changes.

metadata.supportReason: Linear GraphQL API fully supports teams, projects, cycles, and labels. Complete setup automatable.
